# Synthetic transaction dataset: data dictionary

**All data is synthetic.** No real customers, accounts, devices or banking data. Generated by `generator.py` (seed 42, fully reproducible: same seed gives a byte-identical CSV).

Regenerate: `python generator.py --out data/transactions.csv --seed 42 --scale 1.0`
(`--scale` multiplies the number of injected scenarios.)

## Headline numbers

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Rows | 129,675 |
| Window | 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-14 (45 days, includes Diwali on 2026-11-08) |
| Accounts | about 2,090 internal accounts (customers, merchants, businesses, mules, dormant mules) plus external IDs (`EMP`, `BIL`, `ATM`, `POS-`) |
| Fraud rows (`is_fraud=1`) | 1,543 (1.19%) |
| AML-pattern rows (`is_aml_pattern=1`) | 1,693 (1.31%) |
| Benign edge-case rows (`is_edge_case=1`) | 5,383 |
| Fraud / AML overlap | 0 rows (a transaction is one or the other) |

## Columns

First 10 are the shared Transaction schema from the master brief. The rest are ground truth for training and evaluation only; never feed them to a model as features.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `txn_id` | `T000001`... in time order |
| `timestamp` | ISO 8601, no timezone, sorted ascending |
| `sender_id`, `receiver_id` | `ACCxxxx` internal accounts; `EMPxxx` employer, `BILxxx` biller, `ATMxxx` ATM (external, no balance) |
| `amount` | INR |
| `channel` | UPI, CARD, NEFT, IMPS, RTGS, WALLET, ATM, NACH |
| `merchant_category` | transfer, groceries, food, fuel, shopping, travel, entertainment, healthcare, electronics, jewellery, education, utilities, rent, emi, salary, pension, wholesale, atm_withdrawal, gambling, crypto_exchange, donation, property_escrow, refund |
| `device_id` | `D####A/B` own device, `D####N` upgraded phone, `DT####` trip device, `DX###` attacker device, `DR###` mule-ring shared device, `POS-ACC####` terminal, `ATM###`; blank for some external credits and automatic debits |
| `location` | City, or `Online` for card-not-present; blank in a few rows |
| `sender_balance_before` | Balance just before the debit. Blank when the sender is external (salary credits). Never below `amount` |
| `is_fraud` | 1 if this single transaction is fraudulent |
| `is_aml_pattern` | 1 if the row is part of a laundering pattern |
| `pattern_type` | `normal` or the pattern name (see below) |
| `scenario_id` | Groups every row of one injected scenario (blank for ordinary rows). A scenario can include a legitimate anchor row, for example the home-city purchase before an impossible-travel fraud |
| `is_edge_case` | 1 for a benign look-alike or data-quality case |
| `edge_case_type` | Which edge case (see below) |

## Fraud patterns (`is_fraud=1`)

| `pattern_type` | Rows | What it looks like |
|---|---|---|
| `card_testing` | 773 | 10-25 card-not-present debits in minutes, first ones under ₹10, bot device, often one large charge at the end |
| `slow_drip` | 188 | 6-12 small debits (₹900-2,400) to one new beneficiary over 1-3 weeks. Own device, normal hours. Hardest case for anomaly models |
| `odd_hour_spike` | 157 | 3-6 debits between 1 and 4 AM to gambling, crypto, jewellery, electronics |
| `account_takeover` | 148 | New device and far city, 3-8 rapid drains of 30-65% of balance, funds then forwarded by mules |
| `app_scam` | 94 | Authorised push payment: victim's own device and city, daytime, large share of balance to a mule. Often a senior |
| `impossible_travel` | 93 | Card used in home city, then 1,000+ km away within 5-40 minutes |
| `high_value_anomaly` | 90 | One-off large transfer (50-90% of balance) to a new beneficiary, often on a new device |

## AML patterns (`is_aml_pattern=1`)

| `pattern_type` | Rows | What it looks like |
|---|---|---|
| `structuring` | 391 | 6-14 transfers of ₹45,000-49,999 from one account, in hours (fast) or over 3-6 days (slow) |
| `fan_in` / `fan_out` | 341 / 182 | 10-30 accounts pay one mule within about 30 hours, which then splits 95% across 5-15 accounts |
| `pass_through` | 332 | Chains of 3-5 mules forwarding 93-99% of the amount within 2-25 minutes; some end at a crypto or gambling merchant. Also the onward hops of fraud proceeds |
| `smurfing` | 237 | 8-16 different senders each send ₹44,000-49,999 to one collector |
| `circular_flow` | 162 | Rings of 3-6 accounts passing ₹2.5-9 lakh around, shrinking 0.5-2% per hop, repeated up to 3 loops |
| `dormant_activation` | 48 | Accounts silent for the whole window suddenly receive ₹1-3 lakh several times, then empty out within hours |

Mule rings share `DR###` devices, and attacker `DX###` devices are reused across 9-24 victims, so device-sharing graphs work as an extra signal.

## Benign edge cases (`is_edge_case=1`, label 0): false-positive traps

A good system should score these low or explain why they are not suspicious.

| `edge_case_type` | What it tests |
|---|---|
| `near_threshold_rent`, `exact_threshold_fee` | Legit monthly ₹49,500 rent and ₹50,000 fee; a naive near-threshold rule fires |
| `large_legit_purchase`, `festival_spike` | One-off big purchases, Diwali shopping surge |
| `traveller_new_location` | New city, sometimes a new device, travel-heavy spending |
| `night_shift_worker` | Regular 0-5 AM activity |
| `charity_fan_in` | Hundreds of donors to one account in a day (benign fan-in) |
| `payroll_fanout` | Business pays many staff on salary day (benign fan-out) |
| `friends_settlement_cycle` | Roommates settle small amounts in a loop (benign cycle) |
| `escrow_pass_through` | Large property money forwarded after 1-3 days |
| `penny_drop_verification` | ₹1 test payment before a real transfer |
| `account_closure_drain` | Whole balance swept out (drain ratio 1.0) |
| `duplicate_retry` | Same payment repeated within seconds by a gateway retry |
| `refund_reversal` | Merchant returns money to the customer |
| `device_upgrade` | Legit switch to a new phone |
| `new_account_cold_start`, `one_time_account`, `dormant_reactivation` | No history: first transactions of a new account, accounts with a single transaction, reactivation after 35+ silent days |
| `missing_metadata` | Random blank device or location |

## Notes and limitations

- Balances are simulated by replaying all events in time order. If an injected scenario needs more money than the account holds (for example structuring), the generator assumes unlogged funding (such as cash) and raises the balance, so `sender_balance_before` is never below `amount`.
- The dataset has no protected attributes (name, gender, religion, age).
- Use a **time-based split** for training: for example train on 2026-10-01 to 2026-11-05 and test on 2026-11-06 onward. Random splits leak scenario rows across train and test.
- Fraud rate of 1.19% is realistic for the task but rare; use class weighting and report PR-AUC, not accuracy.
- Patterns are cleaner than real life. Real laundering is noisier, so state this as a limitation in the README.
